newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee gains vs dlr on institutional selling.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee gains vs dlr on institutional selling.

text.p: The Indian rupee gained against the dollar on Friday on improved supply from financial institutional selling the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee ended Friday at 35.67/68 against the day's opening 35.76/78, they said. It traded at a high of 35.68 and a low of 35.765 per dollar during the day, they said.

Dealers said an unexpected supply of dollars helped the rupee move up against the dollar. "There was strong dollar selling by financial institutions," a dealer said. "Banks were already holding long overnight dollar positions anticipating month-end demand."
"Once the institutions started selling and demand failed to materialise, banks scrambled to get out of their positions."
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India bought cash dollars at 35.67 and 35.68 levels.
The market for forward dollars saw little action on Friday, dealers said. The premia for six-month dollars ended Friday at an annualised rate of 10.90 percent, they said.
